key_insight: A deep-learning motion model found that HFpEF is marked by reduced diastolic cardiac motion and that specific genes linked to calcium handling and extracellular matrix remodeling may help explain this dysfunction.
clinical_relevance: These motion biomarkers could improve risk stratification and mechanistic understanding of HFpEF, a common heart failure subtype with few targeted therapies.
method: Analyzed standard cine cardiac MRI from 83,569 UK Biobank participants.
Used image segmentation plus optical flow to derive 32 myocardial and cavity velocity phenotypes across the cardiac cycle.
Linked imaging phenotypes to prognosis, genome-wide associations, and Mendelian randomization analyses.
evidence_signal: In a pragmatically defined HFpEF subgroup, mid- and late-diastolic velocities were reduced, higher systolic left ventricular myocardial velocity was associated with lower mortality, and genome-wide analysis identified 12 associated risk loci.
watch_item: Findings are largely observational and based on UK Biobank-derived phenotypes, so external validation and clinical deployment testing are still needed.
paper_title: Deep learning cardiac motion analysis reveals the dynamic pathophysiology and genetic architecture of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
